content: I want to build an app to save and manage bookmarks.

The baseline specification is drafted. Per our Spec-Driven workflow, **this is a review gate** — nothing gets planned or built until you approve the spec. Here's what I've written for your review.

---

## 📋 Spec Gate 1 — Bookmark Manager

**File:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/spec.md`

### What the app does (in plain terms)
A personal web app to **save, find, and organize bookmarks**. Three prioritized slices, each usable on its own:

- **P1 — Save a bookmark:** paste an address, it's stored with a title and add-date; invalid addresses are rejected; missing titles are derived.
- **P2 — Browse, search & open:** newest-first list, keyword search across title/address/tags, click to open the original page in a new tab, friendly empty states.
- **P3 — Organize & edit:** edit title/notes/tags, tag-based filtering, delete with a confirmation step, duplicate-address warning.

### How we'll know it's good (success criteria)
- Save a bookmark in **under 15 seconds**
- Find one among **100+** entries in **under 10 seconds**
- Search/filter updates in **under 1 second** at up to **1,000** bookmarks
- **Zero data loss** across restarts

### Key assumptions I made (so we're not blocked)
- **Single-user, personal use** for v1 — no login/accounts
- **Web app** (matches this environment) — not a mobile app or browser extension
- **Manual entry** — no browser import or one-click capture in v1

### ❓ Two scope decisions worth your confirmation
| # | Question | My default |
|---|----------|-----------|
| **Q1** | Single private collection (no login), or user accounts so multiple people keep separate collections? | Single-user, no login |
| **Q2** | Is manual entry enough for v1, or is importing existing browser bookmarks / one-click capture required? | Manual entry only |

---

**Your move:**
- ✅ **Approve as-is** (I'll keep both defaults) → I proceed to the **plan** gate, or
- ✍️ **Adjust** — answer Q1/Q2 or request any other changes, and I'll revise the spec before we plan.

I won't start planning or writing any code until you give the go-ahead.

Please revise it before planning.

For Q1, keep it single-user with no login.

For Q2, I do need import from a standard browser-bookmarks HTML file, preserving titles, tags, and dates. I’d also like export in that same format. One-click browser capture can wait.

A few important behaviours are missing or need correcting:

- Saving should automatically collect the page title, description, favicon, and preview image, while letting me edit the title and description before or after saving.
- Saving an address that already exists should take me to the existing bookmark to edit it, not merely warn me.
- I should be able to edit the address itself as well as the title, description, note, and tags. Existing tags should be suggested as I type.
- Search should include titles, descriptions, notes, and addresses, be case-insensitive, support `#tag`, exact quoted phrases, and AND/OR/NOT with parentheses.
- I need unread/read-later and archived views. Archiving must be reversible and separate from permanent deletion; archived items should stay out of the normal list and search.
- I need sorting beyond newest-first, plus selecting several bookmarks—or everything matching the current view—to tag, mark read/unread, archive, or delete together.
- Notes should support formatted Markdown when viewed.
- Please include saved filters combining a search with included or excluded tags.
- Each saved page should have a local snapshot, with PDFs stored as PDFs, plus an option to preserve it through the Internet Archive.
- The list should show the description and favicon as well as the title and tags.
- I’d like basic display preferences such as default sorting, number of items shown, and font size.

Please update the scenarios and success criteria so these behaviours are clear, then bring the revised specification back for approval.

### The approach in brief
- **One Node.js 24 process** (Express) serving a **React + Vite** frontend and a JSON API on `0.0.0.0:4000` — one port, matching the review environment.
- **SQLite** (`better-sqlite3`) for data; **snapshot files on disk**.
- **Save is fast, enrichment is async**: metadata (title/description/favicon/preview) and snapshot capture run in a background queue so the save itself stays well under 15s.
- **Snapshots** exactly as you specified: web pages → **self-contained single HTML** via SingleFile + the image's Chromium; PDFs → **downloaded as PDF**. Internet Archive is an explicit, best-effort per-bookmark action.
- **Search** uses a **hand-written boolean parser** — chosen specifically so your two rules are guaranteed: text + `#tag` ⇒ both must match, and `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` are literal words when quoted. Documented with worked examples in the search-grammar contract.
- **Import/export** = classic **Netscape bookmark format** (folders↔tags, dates preserved, duplicates skipped).
- **Testing**: Vitest (unit/API) for the tricky pure logic, Playwright **pinned to 1.61.0** for E2E (no second browser download).

### Notable decisions worth your eye
- **Frontend = React + Vite** (built ahead of time; `npm start` only serves). If you'd prefer something lighter (e.g. server-rendered + htmx) or a different framework, now's the moment.
- **Constitution check**: the project constitution is an unratified template with no defined principles, so there are no gates to enforce — noted as PASS. Say the word if you'd like me to draft a real constitution first.

## 🧭 Plan Gate (revised) — save experience corrected

**Plan:** `specs/001-bookmark-manager/plan.md` (+ research, data-model, contracts, quickstart updated to match)

### What changed

**1. Review the auto-collected details *before* committing** — the save is now a two-step flow:
- **Preview step** (`POST /api/bookmarks/preview`) — collects title, description, favicon, preview image **synchronously** and returns them for you to review and edit. **Nothing is saved yet.**
- **Commit step** (`POST /api/bookmarks`) — persists the **reviewed** title/description.

**2. Fits the 15-second target** — the preview fetch uses a **bounded ~8s timeout**. If the page can't be read promptly, preview returns **fallback details** (host-derived title, empty description) so you can save immediately and edit later.

**3. Snapshot stays in the background** — it's now the *only* deferred work.

**4. Background can never overwrite your title/description — hard rule** — the snapshot job writes **only** snapshot fields (`snapshotType`/`snapshotStatus`/`snapshotPath`), and favicon/preview *only if still empty*. It is structurally forbidden from touching `title` or `description`, so anything you entered or edited is safe. This is stated as an explicit constraint in `research.md` (Decision 11) and enforced in the data model.

### Where it's reflected
| Artifact | Update |
|----------|--------|
| `research.md` | Decision 5 rewritten (collect-before-commit + fallback); Decision 11 rewritten (background = snapshot only + no-overwrite rule) |
| `data-model.md` | `title`/`description` marked "never modified by background jobs"; `metadataStatus` → `collected`/`fallback` |
| `contracts/openapi.yaml` | New `/api/bookmarks/preview`; commit endpoint clarified; enum fixed |
| `plan.md` | Summary, dependencies, structure, traceability |
| `quickstart.md` | Validation scenario 1 rewritten (review, fallback, no-overwrite check) |

Implementation is complete. Here's the final report.

## ✅ Implementation Complete — Bookmark Manager

All **73 tasks** across the 10 user stories plus Setup, Foundational, and Polish are implemented and marked `[x]` in `tasks.md`. Built via the full SDD gate sequence you approved: **spec → plan → tasks → implement**.

### What was built
- **Backend** (Node.js 24 + Express + SQLite/`better-sqlite3`): 22 modules — routes, services (search parser/evaluator, URL normalizer, metadata, snapshot, web-archive, Netscape import/export, filters, preferences), DB layer, and an in-process background queue.
- **Frontend** (React + Vite, built to `dist/`): app shell with hash routing, All/Unread/Archived/Add/Edit/Filters/Import-Export/Preferences views, and shared components (list, row, tag type-ahead, bulk bar, sort, Markdown view).
- **One process** serves the API and SPA on `0.0.0.0:4000`; `.harness/app.json` is set for `kind: application`.

### Your specific requirements — verified working
- **Review-before-commit save** with automatic title/description/favicon/preview, editable, and prompt **fallback** when a page can't be read (validated live).
- **favicon + preview persisted** on commit (test `bookmarks-create` asserts it).
- **Re-saving opens the existing bookmark** — including `http`↔`https`, trailing slash, host case (validated live: same id returned).
- **Search**: text + `#tag` requires both; `AND/OR/NOT` are operators unless quoted (literal); phrases; parentheses; malformed → clear error. Full grammar covered by unit tests + the contract.
- **Snapshots**: self-contained single **HTML** for web pages (captured example.com live via Chromium), **PDFs as PDFs**; background capture **never overwrites** your title/description (dedicated no-overwrite test).
- **Restart persistence**: a process-restart test confirms bookmarks, edits, tags, statuses, filters, preferences, and completed snapshots survive; a **pending snapshot is re-enqueued** on startup.
- Read-later/reversible archive, sort + bulk (incl. select-all-matching), Markdown notes, saved filters, Netscape import/export, and display preferences — all implemented with tests.

### Validation
- **Unit + API tests: 73/73 passing** (`npm test`), covering the high-value logic and the API surface.
- **Playwright E2E** happy-path (add → search → archive) passing.
- **Live end-to-end** checks passed: create/dedup/search/malformed-query/preferences-bounds/import/export/archive, and a real background HTML snapshot.

### Honest notes
1. **`npm test` uses a small retry wrapper** (`scripts/run-tests.mjs`). `better-sqlite3`'s native finalizer intermittently aborts the Vitest worker *at teardown*, after tests report — unrelated to correctness.
